title: Dissecting the Role of Inherited Non-Coding Variants in the Enhancer Architecture of Breast Cancer
text:
Breast cancer remains the most common cancer in women and a leading cause of cancer mortality
worldwide, with persistent disparities in incidence and outcomes. This project will define how genetic variation
across individuals and populations alters FOXA1-mediated enhancer activity and how inflammatory signaling
further amplifies these regulatory differences. The resulting insights will support the development of predictive
biomarkers and inform precision-medicine strategies to reduce treatment failure and improve patient outcomes

title: Discerning the Mechanisms of Compaction and Apical Domain Formation in Early Embryos.
text:
The proposed research will uncover how embryos organize their first cell layers and make their first decisions
about cell types, which are essential to laying the groundwork for life. By studying these early events, we aim
to understand the mechanisms that culminate in successful pregnancies and to unearth new knowledge that
will inform regenerative medicine. This knowledge has the potential to significantly improve health outcomes
related to fertility, aberrant development, and organ dysfunction, demonstrating the positive impact of our work.

title: Novel Mechanisms for Lung Cancer-associated Thrombosis
text:
Individuals with lung cancer are at an elevated risk of developing DVT with limited treatment options. Using
unbiased transcriptomics of G-CSF exposed human neutrophils, we discovered enhanced glycolysis,
inflammasome activation, concomitant with increased expression of key glycolytic enzyme PGK1. In this
proposal, we will define the mechanisms by which neutrophil specific PGK1 promotes DVT severity in lung
cancer with the ultimate objective to establish therapeutic approaches to improve DVT outcomes in lung
cancer.

title: Deep Learning Technology for Rapid Morphological and Quantitative Imaging of Knee Pathology
text:
This project will develop, optimize and evaluate a rapid 5-minute knee MRI protocol consisting of all clinical
sequences and additional T2 mapping sequences, enabling imaging of the whole knee for both morphological
and quantitative assessment of joint pathology. The proposed technique explores the acceleration of knee MRI
by leveraging the latest deep learning technology combined with novel image acquisition and automatic
processing. Given the increasing prevalence of knee osteoarthritis and the overall cumulative knee injuries, our
novel imaging methods would offer a unique opportunity to improve joint health care, reduce healthcare costs,
and benefit a large population that suffers knee pain and joint discomfort in the United States.

title: Susceptibility and adverse health outcomes related to weather-sensitive events among older Medicare beneficiaries with Alzheimer and Dementia
text: The public health burden of exposures of extreme temperatures and air pollution including wildfire smoke with the rapidly increasing burden of older persons with Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and related dementias (ADRD) in the US make the intersection of these conditions a critical public health concern. We propose a national study to estimate risk of mortality, hospital admissions and readmissions, and a novel patient-centered outcome of days at home from exposure to heat including heat waves and air pollution including wildfire smoke, as well as co-occurring heat and air pollution events, for the older US population (>65y) with AD/ADR; we will assess multiple facets of vulnerability based on individual- and community-level factors (e.g., sex, frailty, chronic conditions). This work will involve the use of state-of-the-science methodologies including machine learning algorithms and causal inference methods, and we will disseminate exposure data, methods, and statistical code, making them publicly available free of charge.

title: ATIC is a novel molecular target in diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma
text:
Diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG) is an incurable brainstem malignancy in children with
median survival less than 1 year and 5-year overall survival only 2 percent. Little progress has been made in treating this
deadly disease due to its inoperable location and treatments aimed at targets defined in adult gliomas. We recently
generated a metabolic profile for DIPG elucidating key differentially altered pathways in this tumor. Our long-term goal
is to significantly improve the overall survival of children with DIPG by identifying novel therapeutically amenable
targets.

title: The role of EWSR1 at the centromere
text:
Statement
Our studies will make important contributions to help clarify the mechanisms of centromere maintenance and
specify the role of EWSR1 in centromere function and chromosome segregation, which will lead to insights
relevant to health and disease, including cancer, birth defects, and developmental disorders such as Down
syndrome.

title: Elucidating biophysical mechanisms for force sensing and control using non-equilibrium statistical mechanics and AI
text:
In this work we use non-equilibrium statistical mechanics frameworks, artificial intelligence tools and
computer simulations to predict and model how various biological systems and processes, such as those
responsible for cell shape and locomotion, and cell signaling perform their jobs robustly.

title: Structural Bioinformatics of Proteins and Protein Complexes and Applications to Cancer Biology
text:
Proteins function through their three-dimensional structures, which may be determined experimentally or through
computational methods. The latter has undergone huge advances just in the last year. In this project, we will
bring experimental and computed protein structures to problems in cancer biology through statistical study of
protein families critical to cancer development and therapeutics and collaborative work with Fox Chase
colleagues working in many fields of experimental and clinical cancer research.

title: Identifying Ecological Drivers of Dysbiosis in the Female Reproductive Tract
text:
The vaginal microbiome is an essential barrier to disease that is compromised in 1/3 of all women. Our
understanding of the ecological drivers that control vaginal microbiota composition is limited, and as such we
lack effective treatments to restore homeostasis in women suffering from dysbiosis. Here, we propose to
elucidate the host and bacterial factors that contribute to vaginal dysbiosis to reveal new therapeutic targets that
bolster a protective vaginal microbiota community and strengthen this important, yet understudied aspect of
women’s health.

title: Targeting TRAPPC11 as a therapeutic in inherited dilated cardiomyopathy
text:
Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a common cause of heart failure with a severe lack of therapeutics, creating a
significant clinical burden. TRAPPC11 encodes an integral trafficking protein whose knockdown rescues
contractile dysfunction in DCM patient-derived human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes.
This project explores the therapeutic efficacy of targeting TRAPPC11 knockdown in mice, various genetic DCM,
and through loss of function single nucleotide polymorphisms to generate a translational and mechanistic
rationale for targeting TRAPPC11 in DCM.

title: Defining a Dystonia Specific Spiking Signature in Cerebellar Nuclei Cells
text:
The pathophysiological causes for the involuntary and debilitating muscle over - and co-contractions in dystonia
are poorly understood, despite it being the third most common movement disorder in the United States. Animal
models for dystonia point toward a mechanistic role for the inception of dystonia -like motor deficits stemming
from dysfunction of cerebellar nuclei neurons, which connect the cerebellar circuit to other regions in the motor
circuit that are also involved in dystonia. I will use quantitative electrophysiology in genetic, pharmacological,
and optogenetic mouse models of dystonia to determine if a dystonia-specific signature in the spiking activity of
cerebellar nuclei neurons drives the disease and track how this signature arises during aberrant circuit
maturation.

title: Ultrafast bioimaging
text:
The PI proposes to develop an intelligent ultrafast bioimaging program which could open a
new area of investigation and lead to a series of fundamental scientific discoveries.

title: Cholinergic Dysregulation of Cognitive Flexibility in Cocaine Use Disorder
text:
Cocaine use disorder is characterized by compulsive, inflexible drug-seeking behavior driven in part by
disrupted communication within the striatum. This project will determine how cocaine self-administration alters
cholinergic signaling and circuit interactions that support flexible decision-making, and how these changes
impair the ability to update behavior during reversal learning. By identifying neural mechanisms that can be
targeted to restore cognitive flexibility, this work may guide the development of new interventions to reduce
cocaine use and improve treatment outcomes.

title: Tech-Train-Dissem Core
text: TRAINING AND DISSEMINATION: PROJECT SUMMARY The field of Immunoengineering is a rapidly growing combination of two diverse, complex fields: engineering and immunology. In each, there is a widespread lack of fundamental understanding of the other. JH-TIE will continue to take a leadership position in breaking down barriers between the fields by providing broad dissemination of immunoengineering principles, tools, and technical advances and facilitating collaborations between immunologists and engineers. The P41 mechanism is an ideal opportunity to overcome the divide between researchers in immunology and engineering. JH-TIE will make the lexicon, approach, and tools of immunoengineering accessible to a wide array of researchers; our vision is to become a hub and thought leader for immunoengineering. Our researchers will disseminate our work through scholarly publications, workshops, conference posters and presentations, and our dedicated JH-TIE website for use by collaborative participants worldwide. JH-TIE will continue to host our Translational Immunoengineering Workshop and Course every January and extend our educational programming through the year via our new Translational Immunoengineering Seminar Series. Also, new in this grant cycle, we will be running an innovative combined educational and hackathon initiative through JH-TIE (“Frameshift”) that will offer opportunities for in-person dissemination of JH-TIE technologies and serve to nucleate new Collaborative and Service Projects. With an integrated immunology-and-engineering approach, we can address a myriad of challenges in a wide variety of applications such as cancer immunotherapy and tissue engineering. Blurring the lines between immunology and engineering offers the opportunity for unique synergy in medicine. Our education, training, and dissemination goals will help ensure the impacts of JH-TIE extend well beyond our immediate research goals and persist as our message and trainees propagate.

title: The oral glucocorticoid system in oral carcinogenesis and its modulation for improved treatment outcomes
text:
Oral cancer is a major public health concern, with 58,450 cases diagnosed in the US each year. Since current
preventive and therapeutic approaches have not significantly improved oral cancer outcomes and could
potentially be harmful, it is essential that alternative approaches to treatment be developed and tested. We will
determine the impact of glucocorticoids and glucocorticoid signaling on oral cancer development, and the effects
of the chemopreventive agent gallic acid on this pathway during oral cancer chemoprevention.

title: 2026 In Vivo Ultrasound Imaging Gordon Research Conference and Gordon Research Seminar
text:
Ultrasound imaging, also known as ultrasonography, is the most widespread and accepted clinical imaging
modality and offers diagnostic information throughout the human lifespan, starting prebirth. While its dynamic
and scholarly research community continually improves image quality, it also develops new ways to benefit from
this exciting modality that involves in vivo biomedical ultrasound applications. This meeting will bring together
scientists and trainees from a wide range of backgrounds to discuss and further ultrasonography so that those
in need can benefit from lung ultrasound, virtual biopsies, immunotherapy and more, and will soon be seeing
wearable ultrasound to understand better how daily activities, ailments, and disorders impact our bodies.

title: Novel Immunotherapy Targeting Local and Systemic Immunity for Treatment of Ocular Surface Squamous Neoplasia
text:
Relevance to Public Health. Ocular surface neoplasia (OSSN) can cause permanent corneal injury and
blindness and there are no FDA approved treatments for OSSN. Multiple different off- label treatments are
currently used, some with significant side effects. In this proposal, we will evaluate a new type of ocular
immunotherapy for OSSN, which we have shown induces tumor regression in a horse OSSN model, and
conduct studies to better understand the mechanisms of how this new immunotherapy works to help advance
this treatment for patients with OSSN.

title: Project 1. Optimization and in vivo evaluation of HIV-1 Env trimer sortase A-conjugated nanoparticles
text: ABSTRACT-PROJECT 1 Previous vaccines have been unable to elicit HIV-1 broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) in humans. Two of the reasons for this failure are that bnAb precursor B cells are often rare and that the B cell receptors on those rare B cells require extensive somatic mutation to evolve into high-affinity bnAbs. A subset of these somatic mutations—termed improbable mutations—have a low probability of being made by the somatic mutation machinery due to codon bias and positioning of somatic mutation recognition motifs. Our central hypothesis for eliciting bnAbs is that immunogens must have a higher affinity for Abs with the required improbable mutations than for Abs lacking these key mutations. Moreover, we hypothesize that mutation-guided vaccine design will need to engage low-affinity rare bnAb precursors and, then, through immunization with sequential immunogens, select for Abs acquiring the somatic changes requisite for a broad neutralization phenotype. We and others have observed that multimerizing HIV-1 envelope (Env) immunogens on nanoparticles (NPs) can increase Ab titers and affinity maturation of HIV-1 bnAb lineages. However, Env is unstable and can adopt non-native conformations on the surface of NPs, leading to undesired Ab responses. Additionally, NPs bearing HIV-1 envelope can be of low protein yield. To overcome these pitfalls, we have developed an innovative, rapid platform that uses the enzyme sortase A to covalently link well-folded, cleaved Env trimers to self- assembling ferritin protein NPs. These sortase A-conjugated NPs (scNPs) maintain near-native Env trimer conformation, allowing avid selection of improbable mutations in evolving bnAb lineages. In humanized mice, we used a scNP displaying an engineered Env trimer called CH505.M5 G458Y to select for a key improbable mutation required for maturation of the 8ANC131/CH235 class of CD4 binding site (CD4bs) bnAbs. The same scNP elicited CD4bs monoclonal neutralizing Abs and serum neutralizing Abs in nonhuman primates (NHPs). To further guide these Abs to develop neutralization breadth, we have generated a boosting Env trimer scNP immunogen called CH505.TF scNP and have a third boosting Env under development. In CH505.M5 G458Y scNP-primed NHPs, CH505 TF scNP immunization boosts neutralizing Ab titers against multiple CH505 viruses. This IPCAVD will generate a CH505 TF scNP boosting immunogen and a second sequential Env trimer scNP boosting immunogen for a Phase I trial. In Specific Aim 1, Project 1 will determine an optimal NP boosting regimen to broaden the neutralization capacity of current CD4bs B cell lineages in humanized mice. In Specific Aim 2, we will compare conjugation efficiency and immunogenicity of scNPs assembled from research-grade or development-run ferritin and sortase A components from Project 2. Lastly, Specific Aim 3 will demonstrate the induction of CD4bs lineages in NHPs using the prime-boost strategy and cGMP scNPs proposed for the Phase I trial. The impact of this Project is that it will define and demonstrate the effectiveness of a novel, optimal NP vaccine regimen to expand and affinity mature 8ANC131/CH235 class CD4bs bnAbs.

title: The role of mitochondrial regulation in cell lineage specification and function
text:
Mitochondria are essential organelles in all eukaryotic cells, and their dysfunction has severe consequences in
development and diseases. Mitochondria are highly dynamic through biogenesis, trafficking, changing
morphology and targeted removal. Our research seeks fundamental understanding of the regulatory biology of
mitochondria under normal physiology focusing on the crosstalk among mitochondrial dynamics, mitochondrial
functions, cellular metabolism and signaling.
